elements.element: Customer may assign without Vendor consent to an affiliate
elements.evidence: "The Company may assign this Agreement without HDI's consent to an affiliate"

elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets
elements.evidence: "or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all of its assets"

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent
elements.evidence: "HDI may not assign this Agreement without the Company's prior written consent"

elements.element: Vendor consent standard: not to be unreasonably withheld
elements.evidence: "such consent not to be unreasonably withheld"

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor
elements.evidence: "and in no event to a competitor of the Company"

elements.element: No Vendor termination right on Customer's change of control
elements.evidence: No change-of-control termination right appears in Section 10.3; the condition is absent, so no limitation is required ("but no other person shall acquire or have any rights under this Agreement")

elements.element: Mutual right to assign to successors with written notice
elements.evidence: Insertion gives Customer a consent-free successor right but imposes consent on HDI; no written-notice mechanic ("without HDI's consent" / "without the Company's prior written consent")

elements.element: Consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld
elements.evidence: "such consent not to be unreasonably withheld"

reasons: The inserted sentence pair supplies every atomic element of the preferred position: Customer affiliate/successor assignment without consent, Vendor assignment only with Customer's prior written consent not unreasonably withheld, and an absolute bar on assignment to a Customer competitor.
No Vendor termination right on Customer change of control exists in the clause, so that conditional requirement is satisfied by absence rather than requiring new language.

The redline is a concise two-sentence insertion after the existing binding-effect sentence; the original successors-and-assigns language and the 'no other person' limitation remain fully effective, with no undefined terms or dangling mechanics introduced.
Fallback is not independently satisfied (no mutual written-notice successor mechanic), but the locked target is preferred, which is met, so the levels are not mixed.
